header:
How Apple makes money
from the App Store

lines.text: Apple takes up to 30 cents of every app dollar.
lines.say: Apple takes up to thirty cents of every app dollar.

lines.text: The standard US App Store cut is 30%, or 15% for developers under $1 million a year. Europe's is lower now.
lines.say: The standard US cut is thirty percent, or fifteen for developers earning under a million a year. Europe's is lower now.

lines.text: On a $9.99 purchase: 30% is $3.00, so the developer keeps $6.99.
lines.say: On a nine ninety-nine purchase, thirty percent is three dollars, so the developer keeps six ninety-nine.

lines.text: Apple's Services, including the App Store, iCloud and ads, made $109.2 billion in fiscal 2025.
lines.say: Apple's services, including the App Store, iCloud and ads, made a hundred nine point two billion dollars in fiscal twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: That's up from $46.3 billion in fiscal 2019.
lines.say: That's up from forty-six point three billion in fiscal twenty nineteen.

lines.text: Services are far more profitable: a 75.4% gross margin, vs 36.8% on devices.
lines.say: Services are far more profitable: a seventy-five point four percent gross margin, versus thirty-six point eight percent on devices.

lines.text: So services were 26% of sales, but about 42% of gross profit.
lines.say: So services were twenty-six percent of sales, but about forty-two percent of gross profit.

lines.text: Plot twist: an Apple-funded study says over 90% of money flowing through apps paid no commission.
lines.say: Plot twist: an Apple-funded study says over ninety percent of money flowing through apps paid Apple no commission.

post.ig:
Apple takes up to 30 cents of every app dollar.
The standard US App Store cut is 30%, or 15% for developers earning under $1 million a year (Europe's standard rate is lower as of Oct 2026).
Apple's Services, including the App Store, brought in $109.2 billion in fiscal 2025, with a 75.4% gross margin vs 36.8% on devices.
Services were 26% of sales but about 42% of gross profit.
Sources: Apple FY2025 Form 10-K, Apple Developer.
News and education, not financial advice.
